INDEPENDENT AUDIT: FINITE CONTROL, NOISY GAUSSIAN READS, AND A GENERAL FIRST STAGE
Scientific-computation branch, 2026-10-30.

VERDICT

The proposed exact noisy replay reduction is valid under the access contract
below. The general first-stage decomposition is also valid. The essential
corrections are explicit decoder knowledge, charged control timing, absence
of uncharged correlated actuator side information, and separation of
algorithmic random seeds from the measurement-noise innovations. The replay
freeze includes the innovations only as a mathematical coupling; the posterior
calculation must never reveal those innovations to the predictor.

The intended output is at the controller, or at a decoder retaining the same
first-stage information. The actuator only implements sensing directions and
returns its readouts. This audit does not broaden the theorem to an
actuator-only predictor.

1. CONTRACT THAT MAKES THE THEOREM PRECISE

V~N(0,I_n). C is an R^n-valued random variable independent of V with
E||C||^2<infinity. The controller knows C. The actuator initially has no
C-dependent information except a declared public context Z, if present.
For the unconditional version Z is absent or independent of C.

The actuator can take at most q measurements

  Y_t=u_t^T V+xi_t,  ||u_t||<=1,
  xi_1,...,xi_q iid N(0,s),  s>0.

The innovation sequence is external measurement noise, independent of C,V,
and all algorithmic random seeds. Its realizations are not available to either
party except through the readouts. Directions are predictable from the
actuator's received control bits, previous legal readouts and its algorithmic
seeds. Feedback can return any function of these readouts and seeds, including
the entire readout record, but no extra information about V.

The control protocol has at most B binary controller branches on every path,
so a fixed replay has at most 2^B complete control words. Fixed-length padded
words with a public state deciding when to request the next bit are a
convenient equivalent implementation. Any controller-dependent timing,
stopping, measurement requests, addresses, metadata, or message boundaries
must be included in this control alphabet. A bare payload-length bound with
free termination is insufficient.

Hard q and B bounds hold. Counterfactual branches can be totalized by stopping
or capping at q reads and B bits. This changes no actual

P1: EARLY INFORMATION AS A DESCRIPTION OF THE REMAINING EXPERIMENT
Ordinary proof and synthesis, 30 October 2026 UTC.

Status: a foundational resource characterization and an explicit construction.
The theorems are proved here. Historical priority is unresolved. No physical
sensor, universal representation learner, or practical runtime advantage is
claimed. Earlier p1_next and p1_research artifacts are preserved unchanged.

1. THE CAPABILITY

The scientific objective is prediction at a prescribed final squared error,
including the information needed to choose a measurement. The opportunity is
that a large family of task coefficients can have a short nonlinear
description, even when no fixed low-dimensional linear representation retains
the target. Early measurements may acquire that description. A second-stage
actuator can then compute an appropriate aggregate while keeping its large
input local. Whether that aggregate is genuinely accessible remains a separate
question; software arithmetic and physical programming are not free.

The new organizing object is the distribution of the residual task coefficient
and its distortion under permitted measurement designs. A covariance matrix
determines all fixed-experiment risks in the conditional-linear setting below,
but does not determine the value of finite control. This is a precise limit on
the fixed-experiment covariance interface developed in the earlier campaign.

2. EXACT FINITE-CONTROL VALUE, INCLUDING NOISY INTERACTION

Let C in R^m have any known square-integrable law, and let V~N(0,I_m) be
independent of C. The target is C^T V. The controller initially knows C. The
final predictor retains C and receives the complete legal readout transcript.
The actuator has no additional information about C, and sees V only through
at most q unit-power linear reads (row norm at most one), each with independent
N(0,s) noise, s>0. An optimal design can use unit rows: increasing a row's
power only improves its information and leaves its scalar cost unchanged.

Controller bits, readouts and direction choices can be arbitrarily interleaved.
The actuator can choose directions from its past readouts, received bits and
independent seeds. The controller may receive readouts freely in this theorem;
return bandwidth is a separate resource. Every C-dependent actuator
distinction, including timing, requests and stopping, is charged
